title: Subspace or relative topology
terms: subspace topology; relative topology; relatively open; relatively closed.

exposition.text:
For S ⊆ X, the subspace topology is {S ∩ U : U open in X}. A relatively closed subset similarly
equals S ∩ F for a closed subset F of X. Relative openness or closedness always depends on the
stated ambient space.
If S itself is open in X, every relatively open subset of S is open in X; the analogous closed
statement also holds. In subspaces of R, isolated points become open singletons even though
singletons are never open in the ambient real line.
S X
For A ⊆ S ⊆ X, relative closure satisfies A = S ∩ A . Interior has no such general intersection
formula; a thin set may have empty ambient interior while being open in itself. Every relatively
open subset of S is ambient open exactly when S itself is ambient open.

question.text:
Let S = [0, 1] ∪ {2} have the subspace topology from R. Which subset is both open and closed in
S?
(A) [0, 1/2) (B) [0, 1/2] (C) {0} (D) [0, 1] (E) (0, 1)

solution.text:
[0, 1] = S ∩ (−1, 3/2) is relatively open, and it is closed in R, hence in S. The first and
fifth sets omit relative limit points; the second and third are not relatively open at their
nonisolated boundary points.

question.text:
Let S = {0} ∪ {1/n : n ∈ N, n ≥ 1} in R. Which subset is open in S but not closed in S?
(A) {0} (B) {1} (C) S \ {0} (D) {0, 1} (E) ∅

solution.text:
Every 1/n is isolated, so their union S \ {0} is open. It is not closed because 0 is a limit
point. The singleton {1} and the empty set are both open and closed.

question.text:
For S ⊆ R, which condition is equivalent to every relatively open subset of S being open in R?
(A) S is closed in R.
(B) S is open in R.
(C) S is finite.
(D) S is dense in R.
(E) S has the discrete relative topology.

solution.text:
If S is open, each relatively open set S ∩ U is an intersection of two ambient open sets and is
open. Conversely, S is always open in itself, so the stated property applied to S forces S to
be open in R. Relative openness alone does not imply ambient openness.

The irrational boundary point is absent from the subspace. Both the chosen set and its
complement are intersections of Q with ordinary open rays, so both are relatively open.
